headline: BRINSUPRI launch fuels revenue surge, losses narrow
summary_short: Insmed's Q1 2026 revenue jumped 229.6% y/y (+16.0% q/q) to $306.0M on BRINSUPRI's commercial launch, while net loss narrowed 36.3% y/y to $163.6M as R&D and SG&A investment scaled with the launch.
summary_long: Revenue rose 229.6% y/y (+16.0% q/q) to $306.0M, driven by $207.9M of BRINSUPRI net sales in its first full quarter after the August 2025 US approval, plus 5.7% ARIKAYCE growth led by 23.4% international-sales growth. Cost of product revenue rose to $47.4M but fell to 15.5% of revenue (from 22.9%) since BRINSUPRI carries lower manufacturing cost than ARIKAYCE. R&D rose $56.9M y/y on headcount, manufacturing and TPIP clinical spend; SG&A rose $99.7M y/y, mostly professional fees and headcount tied to BRINSUPRI commercialization. Net loss narrowed 36.3% y/y to $163.6M. Cash and equivalents rose to $582.2M (+44.4% y/y); marketable securities fell to $641.3M. No numeric forward guidance was disclosed in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Increase attributable to $207.2M of US commercial BRINSUPRI sales following its August 2025 approval, plus 5.7% ARIKAYCE growth driven by 23.4% international sales growth.

Cost of product revenue fell to 15.5% of revenue from 22.9% because BRINSUPRI has lower manufacturing costs than ARIKAYCE, per the filing; gross profit itself is a derived readout of revenue minus that cost line.

Loss narrowed as revenue growth outpaced expenses, though R&D (+$56.9M, headcount/manufacturing/TPIP) and SG&A (+$99.7M, professional fees and headcount) both rose sharply on BRINSUPRI commercialization.
Tracks the same operating-loss dynamics; not separately reconciled by the company beyond the R&D/SG&A driver list above.
Same basis as EBIT and operating loss; moves with revenue growth against a smaller expense increase.
Narrowed alongside the operating loss; a $47.0M favorable swing in contingent-consideration fair value (lower share price, offset partly by PRV-program reauthorization) also reduced the loss.
Tracks the narrower net loss; weighted average shares rose to 215.5M from 180.9M y/y but did not offset the improvement.

Rose as $265.5M of marketable-securities maturities and $29.5M of financing inflows more than offset $222.7M used in operating activities; combined cash-plus-securities actually fell as securities balances were drawn down.
Unchanged q/q; the sharp y/y decline reflects the 2025 redemption of the 0.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028, completed in Q2 2025. No new borrowing was disclosed this quarter.

q/q decline reflects the $163.6M net loss outweighing $30.3M of option-exercise proceeds and $45.8M of stock-based compensation; the large y/y gain reflects a $823.3M net-proceeds equity offering completed in June 2025.

BRINSUPRI's US launch drove the quarter: revenue more than tripled y/y while losses narrowed, though R&D and SG&A both scaled sharply with commercialization and clinical spend (TPIP external R&D +308% y/y). No numeric guidance was given.
